questions.text: A path leads directly toward a clearly visible entrance along a straight axial route. Which approach type is most source-backed?

options.text: Oblique approach.
Spiral approach.
Frontal approach.
Grid path configuration only.

rationale.correct: TOA 2 defines frontal approach as direct movement to the entrance along a straight axial path.
rationale.takeaway: Approach questions usually ask how the route prepares entry.
rationale.a: An oblique approach changes perspective rather than going straight to the entrance.
rationale.b: A spiral approach prolongs movement around the form.
rationale.d: A grid is a broader path configuration, not this approach type.

questions.explanation: TOA 2 defines frontal approach as direct movement to the entrance along a straight axial path. Approach questions usually ask how the route prepares entry.

questions.text: A visitor circles part of a building before entering, gradually seeing several sides of the form. Which approach type is being used?

options.text: Frontal approach, because every entry route is straight.
Spiral approach, because it prolongs the sequence and emphasizes three-dimensional form.
Static anthropometry, because the route is only body measurement.
Color temperature, because the route changes mood.

rationale.correct: TOA 2 describes spiral approach as prolonging the approach and emphasizing three-dimensional form while moving around it.
rationale.takeaway: Movement around a form is a key cue for spiral approach.
rationale.a: A frontal approach is straight and direct.
rationale.c: Anthropometry addresses body dimensions, not the path type.
rationale.d: Color temperature is not the route configuration.

questions.explanation: TOA 2 describes spiral approach as prolonging the approach and emphasizing three-dimensional form while moving around it. Movement around a form is a key cue for spiral approach.

questions.text: Which statement best matches the source map for path configuration?

options.text: Only spiral paths count as movement paths.
Paths are unrelated to the sequence of spaces.
All movement paths are linear in nature because they start somewhere and proceed through a sequence toward a destination.
Paths apply only to exterior roads and never to interiors.

rationale.correct: TOA 2 states that all paths of movement are linear in nature and lead through a sequence of spaces.
rationale.takeaway: A path can be linear in movement even when configured as radial, spiral, grid, or network.
rationale.a: Spiral is one configuration, not the only path type.
rationale.b: Sequence is central to the source map.

questions.explanation: TOA 2 states that all paths of movement are linear in nature and lead through a sequence of spaces. A path can be linear in movement even when configured as radial, spiral, grid, or network.

questions.text: A ramp is used because the accessible route changes level. Which BP 344 detail is source-backed for the accessible ramp?

options.text: Minimum clear width of 1200 mm and gradient not steeper than 1:20, subject to the cited exceptions/special cases.
Any width is acceptable if the path is attractive.
The ramp can replace all landings and handrails.
Only color contrast is regulated for ramps.

rationale.correct: The 2024 BP 344 source map gives the 1200 mm minimum clear width and 1:20 gradient rule for accessible ramps.
rationale.takeaway: Code claims need exact local-source support.
rationale.b: Aesthetic quality does not replace minimum dimensions.
rationale.c: The source map also includes landings and handrails.
rationale.d: Color/contrast is not the only ramp requirement.

questions.explanation: The 2024 BP 344 source map gives the 1200 mm minimum clear width and 1:20 gradient rule for accessible ramps. Code claims need exact local-source support.

questions.text: A stair serving a typical building has 220 mm risers and 230 mm runs. Which PD 1096 source-backed issue is most direct?

options.text: The stair is automatically correct because it has any rise and run.
The riser exceeds 200 mm and the run is below 250 mm.
The issue is only proxemic personal distance.
The issue is only hue and chroma.

rationale.correct: The PD 1096 local source sets stair rise not exceeding 200 mm and run not less than 250 mm for the cited condition.
rationale.takeaway: Movement-through-space questions can become code questions when stairs, ramps, and corridors are involved.
rationale.c: Personal distance does not replace stair geometry.
rationale.d: Color vocabulary does not resolve stair safety dimensions.

questions.explanation: The PD 1096 local source sets stair rise not exceeding 200 mm and run not less than 250 mm for the cited condition. Movement-through-space questions can become code questions when stairs, ramps, and corridors are involved.
